Transcript of Advertisement inserted into a copy of the basegame.
ETERNAL WINTER Adventure Pack
This Expansion Set Features: - 6 new Level 3 adventures - A 3D ice tower, adding an extra dimension to the gameplay - A new Barbarian hero figure - 8 new Monsters, including Ice Dragon - Roaming Monsters, who materialize in the wilderness, hungry to attack - Wintry weapons and spells -- and flight action!
The battle continues in the frozen winter wastelands. Here, vicious creatures roam the icy landscape, hunting for unprotected prey.
A new Hero - a mighty barbarian - has joined the faithful band in their quest to rescue a kidnapped Prince from the claws of a fierce and covetous dragon. The Prince, the last living soul to know the location of his ancient lost city, is held captive by the dragon in an attempt to force him to surrender his secret.
Can the Heroes defeat the evil dragon in this bitter, icy realm? Or will the beast prevail and pillage the legendary city of its unimaginable riches?
Are you brave enough to enter the icy wilderness of Dungeons & Dragons?
2 - 5 players, Ages 10 and up

name.value: For Hive and Colony: The Great Insect War

item.description:
It was a simple arrangement: The Bee Queen shall rule the skies above the earth, and the Ant Queen shall have sole rule of the land. However, the Bee Queen, sick of controlling a domain consisting of mostly air, has declared war!
The Bees launch the offensive, gathering allies from other varieties of flying insects. The Ants scramble their defenses, drawing on the loyalty of their ground-dwelling friends. But admist the conflict lay the beetles: divided, it is unsure which side(s) they will support.
For Hive and Colony is a microgame of strategic, physical card manipulation. Players will take on either the United Colonies or the Hive Powers. They will deploy their oddly shaped cards to the table, then take turns moving them as indicated. Each insect moves in a slightly different fashion. Flip, rotate, translate, and even divebomb the enemy in a mad rush to capture their queen! To the victor: the whole of the world!
For Hive and Colony is a two player game which plays in about 10 to 20 minutes.
NOTE: The images associated with this game are prototype images. All art is used for example only.

item.description:
Guard the Hive's Golden Treasure! was published on the back of a Honey Nut Cheerios cereal box in 2008. The cereal box comes with a Magic Compass Decoder that is used in playing the game.
From the box:
Guard the Hive's Golden Treasure!
Buzz and his friends want to move the honey that makes Honey Nut Cheerios cereal so delicious across the amber ocean. But Yellow Jack and his crew won't make it easy!
To Play: Help Buzz transport the honey across the ocean or challenge a friend to see who can get there first. To play, flip a coin to determine how many spaces to move. Heads move one space, tails moves two.
When you land on a compass, place your magic compass decoder on the spot and move it back and forth to reveal the symbol for your next move. Use the key to determine the value for each symbol.

item.description:
Turn Details Moving a Bee
Move any one of your Bees one hex in any direction. A Bee cannot move onto a Hex with another Bee.
Flicking a Bee
Flick the Bee with your index finger in any direction. Bees that fall off the board are removed from the game.
Collecting Gems
Collect any Gems the Bee touches (by Moving or Flicking). Place collected Gems in your Reserve on the table top (the reserve is visible to all players).
Playing Gems
Optionally play one Gem per Turn from your Reserve. Gems can either be played immediately, after being picked up, or on a later Turn.
Game End
The player with the last remaining Bee(s) on the board is the winner. This game is based upon the classic Checkers variant Chapayev.
—description from the designer

item.description:
Players take turns doing these 4 Actions on their turn:
Move one of your Bees the First Time, like a queen in chess (a straight-line in any of the 6 directions) as far as they want. Bees can only move through open hexes and stop on open Hexes. So, Bees cannot go through hexes that contain other Bees nor Hexes with Gems
Draw a random Gem from the Bag Place the new Gem on the table next to your other Gem. Gems must always be visible on the table. Place one of your 2 Gems on an open Hex next to where the Bee is located. The open hex must be empty (i.e., it cannot contain another bee, nor a Gem).
Move the same Bee a Second Time based upon the Gem Effect. Each color of Gem causes the Bee to move differently for the second movement. If you cannot move your bee a Second Time, the bee is removed from the game. If you cannot move any of your bees the First Time, you lose.
It is then the next player’s turn
—description from the designer

item.description:
Gameplay
Players take turns moving one Larva at a time. Larva can only move by jumping over other Larvae. Players can jump over their own Larvae or their opponents’ Larvae. To Jump, a Larva must start in the Hex next to the first Larva it jumps overs. To end a Jump, there must be an empty Hex to land in. Each Jump must be in a straight-line. Each Jump is over all Larvae next to each other in the line (i.e., the Jump can be any length until an open Hex). Multiple jumps are allowed in a single turn, as long as there are Larvae to jump over and empty spaces to land on. Larvae cannot jump backward. Larvae are not captured (i.e., no Larvae are removed from the board during the game). In the rare event a player cannot make a move, they must pass their turn. Jumping is not mandatory (i.e. you can stop jumping at any time and do not need to continue jumping
if you do not want to).
Game End
The first player to move all their Larvae into the back two rows, on the opposite side of the board, wins the
game.
This game is based upon the classic game Halma.
—description from the designer

name.value: 蟲蟲蜂房 (虫虫蜂房) Hive (繁簡版)

item.description:
Hive is a strategic game for two players that is not restricted by a board and can be played anywhere on any flat surface. Hive is made up of twenty two pieces, eleven black and eleven white, resembling a variety of creatures each with a unique way of moving.
With no setting up to do, the game begins when the first piece is placed down. As the subsequent pieces are placed this forms a pattern that becomes the playing surface (the pieces themselves become the board). Unlike other such games, the pieces are never eliminated and not all have to be played. The object of the game is to totally surround your opponent's queen, while at the same time trying to block your opponent from doing likewise to your queen. The player to totally surround his opponent's queen wins the game.

item.description:
Can your fleet of numbered bees infiltrate the enemy hive and "buzz" the Queen Bee? Higher numbered bees outrank lower ones. With a single "buzz," or touch, they move remove lesser bees from the hive. At number zero, the Queen Bee is practically defenseless. Protect your Queen Bee from attack! Steer clear of the dreaded fungus! Watch out for the deadly Killer Bee!
Math skills covered: inequalities (greater than, less than), fractions, decimals, negative numbers, and place value.
This game is meant for use in grade 2 mathematics classrooms and beyond. The game is to be played by two players at a time. Players try to protect their queen bee from attack; steer clear of the black fungus; and avoid the deadly killer bee. Each player has nine worker bees with a whole number, fraction, or decimal value, one queen bee, and one killer bee. Players attack other bees of unknown value, and the bee with the higher value survives. Whoever captures their opponent's queen bee wins. Mathematics skills covered include inequalities; fractions; decimals; negative numbers; and place value. The game contains a game board, bee value cards, and playing piece stands.
